findings.batch: A — the noise filter (monitoring that misbehaves for real visitors today)
findings.plain_title: Firefox and Safari send the two known AlphaTab errors to Sentry as crashes
findings.engine_title: Firefox/Safari NH-335 throws bypass noise filter, sent as unhandled
findings.engine_why_it_matters: A Firefox or Safari visitor who opens an ordinary Guitar Pro file can hit NH-335. Measured in Chromium, it fires seven times in one open. In those browsers it reaches Sentry as an unhandled error, because the filter's list holds only V8's wording of the message. SpiderMonkey and JavaScriptCore word the same engine bug differently, so `message.includes(noise.message)` never matches, and the event is scrubbed and sent with GlobalHandlers' `handled: false`. Sentry's Dedupe keeps only the first of a run of identical consecutive throws, so this costs about one report per affected open rather than seven. That still spends the 5,000-a-month quota that decision D2 dropped this noise to protect, and it marks those visits unhandled, so the interim Release Health number falls for non-Chromium visitors only. Nothing goes red: the only end-to-end proof that known noise never reaches Sentry (cases 4 and 6 in error-reporting.e2e.ts) runs in Chromium alone, and the unit tests build their events from the V8 messages. The check that keeps our own errors reaching Sentry is the every-frame-in-ENGINE_BUNDLE condition, not the wording, so matching each engine's wording keeps that promise.
findings.engine_suggested_fix: In web/lib/monitoring/known-engine-noise.ts, match each entry by every engine's wording and leave the every-frame-in-ENGINE_BUNDLE condition as it is. NH-335: accept V8's `(reading 'voices')`, SpiderMonkey's `can't access property "voices"` and JavaScriptCore's `evaluating '….voices'`, for example with one regex per entry: /\(reading 'voices'\)|can't access property "voices"|evaluating '[^']*\.voices'/. NH-338: also accept an exception whose type is `InvalidStateError`, because Gecko words stop-before-start differently. That means adding `type` to NoiseEvent. Add Firefox-shaped and WebKit-shaped events, in `fn@url:line:col` frame form, to known-engine-noise.test.ts. The fix assumes AlphaTab's bug does not depend on the browser, because the throwing code is AlphaTab's own JavaScript. Confirm that once in a real Firefox before trusting the change.
findings.engine_validator: known-engine-noise.ts:32,45-46 (added by this diff) matches only V8's wording via includes, while this Mac's JavaScriptCore (run read-only through osascript -l JavaScript) words the same read as `TypeError: undefined is not an object (evaluating 't.voices')`, Sentry 11.4.0 copies ex.message into exception.value (@sentry/browser esm/prod/eventbuilder.js:7,95-109) and tags onerror events handled:false (globalhandlers.js:49-50), web/ has no ignoreErrors or denyUrls, and both e2e projects use Desktop Chrome (playwright.e2e.config.ts:32,51), so a Safari NH-335 throw would pass beforeSend unfiltered; SpiderMonkey's wording was not checked locally and whether AlphaTab's NH-335 actually fires in Firefox or Safari (the precondition) was not measured.
findings.severity_meaning: P2 = a real problem with a meaningful downside; fix if straightforward
findings.confidence_meaning: 75 = the reviewer inferred it from reading the code; this loop's verifier then ran it (see 'verified'). Here the verifier MEASURED it in real browsers, so treat it as confirmed.
findings.verified: pass — measured against a production build of this branch (fake DSN), in Playwright's Chromium 149, Firefox 148 and WebKit 26.5: Chromium sends neither error; Firefox and WebKit send BOTH NH-335 and NH-338 as level error, handled false (an unhandled crash).
findings.scenario: You open the player in Safari or Firefox, choose an ordinary Guitar Pro file, and it plays fine. In the background, the engine's known NH-335 error is sent to Sentry as an unhandled error, so the owner gets an issue for a bug that is already known. If you press Play and then Pause quickly, NH-338 is sent too, and the health number goes down for Safari and Firefox visitors only, although nothing went wrong for them.
findings.whats_wrong: The known-noise list (web/lib/monitoring/known-engine-noise.ts) holds only Chrome's wording of each error, and matches with `message.includes(...)`. Firefox and Safari word the same two engine errors differently, so the filter never matches there, and Sentry receives each one as an unhandled error. Two more measured details: Safari adds a `stop@[native code]` frame to NH-338, which breaks the rule that EVERY frame must be the engine's; and Firefox, when a debugger is attached (Playwright, or open developer tools), adds async frames from our own React code, with the same effect.
findings.breaks_today: Today a Firefox or Safari visitor who opens an ordinary Guitar Pro file (like guitar-no-percussion.gp) sends one unhandled NH-335 error report, and one who presses Play then Pause quickly sends an unhandled NH-338 report. Measured against a production build with the fake DSN: NH-335 fired on the first open in Firefox 148 and WebKit 26.5, and in each the event reached the recorded envelopes with level error and handled false (mechanism auto.browser.global_handlers.onerror); NH-338 the same. In Chromium neither was sent. Each report uses the 5,000-a-month quota and marks the visit unhandled in Release Health.

findings.after_excerpt:
Each entry gets a `wordings` list built only from the MEASURED messages, and `isKnownMessage` tests them; frames named `[native code]` are left out of the every-frame rule (but at least one engine frame is still required):

  NH-335 wordings:
    /Cannot read properties of undefined \(reading 'voices'\)/        (Chrome)
    /can't access property "voices", .+ is undefined/                  (Firefox)
    /undefined is not an object \(evaluating '[^']*\.voices'\)/       (Safari)
  NH-338 wordings:
    /cannot call stop without calling start first/                      (Chrome, Safari)
    /Start has not been called on this AudioBufferSourceNode/           (Firefox)

  const isKnownMessage = (message: string): boolean =>
    KNOWN_ENGINE_NOISE.some((noise) => noise.wordings.some((wording) => wording.test(message)));

  const frames = (exception.stacktrace?.frames ?? []).filter(
    (frame) => frame.filename !== '[native code]',
  );

The V8 `message` field stays, because the Chromium-only end-to-end cases read it. Six new unit cases use the recorded Firefox and WebKit messages and stacks (16/16 pass).
findings.proposed_fix: Match each known error by every browser's measured wording, and ignore Safari's `[native code]` frame in the every-frame rule.
findings.why_it_works: The rule that protects our own errors is 'every frame is in the engine bundle', not the wording, so widening the wording cannot hide one of our errors: the new unit cases show a single frame of our code still keeps the event, and another property read on undefined (in all three wordings) is still sent.

findings.decision_matrix: criteria (weight): stops false crash reports for real visitors (x3), keeps our own errors reaching Sentry (x3), simplicity (x2), evidence (x1). Option 1: 5,5,4,5 -> 15+15+8+5 = 43. Option 2: 3,5,5,5 -> 9+15+10+5 = 39. Option 3: 5,4,2,1 -> 15+12+4+1 = 32.
findings.decisive_tradeoff: How much of the non-Chrome noise to close versus how far to move from the spec's 'every frame is the engine's' rule.
findings.recommendation: Option 1: it is measured in all three browsers, closes every visitor case, and keeps the rule that protects our own errors. Flip to option 2 if you want the frame rule left exactly as written.
findings.also_fold_in: AR-1 (the 'seven times in one open' comment) lands in the same file; apply it in the same commit.
findings.missing_context: No recorded decision covers other browsers: spec 2.6 and D2 measured the noise in Chromium only, and both e2e projects are Chromium. The reviewer missed two measured facts that make the suggested fix incomplete. (1) WebKit's NH-338 wording already matches the list ('cannot call stop without calling start first.'), but WebKit adds a `stop@[native code]` frame, so the every-frame rule keeps the event and it is sent anyway. (2) In Firefox run by Playwright (a debugger is attached), each stack also holds async frames that show where the engine's listener was set up: our own React code in _next/static. So the every-frame rule keeps NH-335 and NH-338 there even with the right wording. With async stacks turned off (javascript.options.asyncstack false), which is likely how a visitor's Firefox runs without its developer tools open (not checked in a release Firefox), all frames are the engine's and the wording fix is enough. Also, the finding's guess that Gecko's NH-338 needs a match on the InvalidStateError type is not needed: Firefox's measured message is distinct ('AudioScheduledSourceNode.stop: Start has not been called on this AudioBufferSourceNode.').
findings.recorded_decisions: Spec decision D2 (drop known engine noise, one list read by Sentry and the e2e gate) — this fix keeps D2; it only makes the list match other browsers. The spec measured the noise in Chromium only.
findings.triage_decision: Apply — option 1, wording + native-frame rule (leocaseiro, 2026-10-13, round 1). AR-1 folded in; spec section 2.6 records the wordings and Known limits records Firefox with its developer tools open.

findings.batch: B — tests that prove a guard works
findings.plain_title: The token check is never tested the way the build runs it
findings.engine_title: Auth-token build guard never run end to end with a token
findings.engine_why_it_matters: The only test of the script as the build runs it passes SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN='' and expects exit 0. That is also what happens if the entry check (process.argv[1] against import.meta.url) never matches, so the last defence against the production token reaching a browser-downloaded file could be a silent no-op with every test green. The branch that prints the report and sets process.exitCode = 1 (assert-no-auth-token.mjs:61-63) is executed by no test; the function-level tests call tokenLeakReport directly and skip that wiring. Running a copy of the real script from a temp web/scripts/ with a planted leak closes the gap without a production seam, because the script derives WEB from its own location.
findings.engine_suggested_fix: Add two cases to tooling/assert-no-auth-token.test.mjs: copy web/scripts/assert-no-auth-token.mjs into <tmp>/web/scripts/, plant <tmp>/web/public/leak.txt holding the fake token, and spawnSync the copy with SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN set to the fake. Expect status 1, stderr naming public/leak.txt and not containing the token. A clean tree with the same token expects status 0. Keep the existing empty-token case.
findings.engine_validator: tooling/assert-no-auth-token.test.mjs:67-73 is the file's only spawnSync and runs with SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN='', which returns null at web/scripts/assert-no-auth-token.mjs:40 and exits 0 whether or not the argv-versus-import.meta.url entry check at :56-59 matches, so the print-and-exitCode=1 path at :60-63 (both files added by this diff; git grep finds no other test or caller besides the build script) is exercised by nothing, though whether the entry check ever fails to match in a real build (the precondition) was not measured.
findings.severity_meaning: P2 = a real problem with a meaningful downside; fix if straightforward
findings.confidence_meaning: 75 = the reviewer inferred it from reading the code; this loop's verifier then ran it (see 'verified')
findings.verified: pass — the test file starts the script once, with an empty token, which exits 0 whether or not the script's entry check works; the path that fails a production build (print the report, exit 1) runs in no test.
findings.scenario: You change the token check later, for example you move its entry check into a helper, and by mistake the check no longer runs when the build starts the script. Every test stays green, because the only test that starts the script gives it an empty token, and then the script exits 0 anyway. Later another change puts the Sentry token into a page, and the production build still passes and serves the token to every visitor.
findings.whats_wrong: tooling/assert-no-auth-token.test.mjs tests the leak-finding function directly, but runs the SCRIPT only with an empty token. If the script's entry check (`process.argv[1]` against `import.meta.url`) stopped matching, the build would run it, it would check nothing, exit 0, and every test would stay green.
findings.breaks_today: Nothing today; it guards a future edit. Measured: started the way the build starts it, with a fake token and a planted public/leak.txt, the script exits 1 and names the file.
findings.after_excerpt:
Two new cases copy the real script into a temporary web/scripts/ and start it EXACTLY as web's build does — from inside web/, `node scripts/assert-no-auth-token.mjs` — with a made-up token in its environment:
  - a temporary web/public/leak.txt holding the token: exit 1, stderr names public/leak.txt, and the output never contains the token;
  - a clean tree with the same token: exit 0.
(the existing empty-token case stays)
findings.proposed_fix: Add the two cases above to tooling/assert-no-auth-token.test.mjs.
findings.why_it_works: It runs the only path that fails a production build. The bite run proved it: breaking the entry check turns exactly the new leak case red while the 9 other cases stay green.

spike.result: 10/10 pass (relative start, as the build does); bite: only the new leak case fails; prettier and cspell pass (eslint does not lint tooling/*.mjs in this repository).
spike.surprise: The finding's own version (start the copy by an ABSOLUTE path under the system temp folder) FAILS on macOS: the temp folder sits behind a symlink, Node resolves symlinks in import.meta.url but not in process.argv[1], so the entry check never matches and the script exits 0 having checked nothing. The build is safe (it starts the script by a relative path, and the working folder is always a real path), so the spiked test uses the build's own form.

findings.recommendation: Apply: tests only, no runtime change, and it pins the last guard between the token and a browser.
findings.missing_context: The gap is already known: the implementation ledger lists it as a deferred minor for Task 2 ("the exit-1 CLI path has no test (only the empty-token exit 0 run); reviewer's probe shows it works"). No decision says to leave it untested, and the plan's commit table claims Task 2 proves "a leaked token fails the build". The finding adds a concrete fix. The spike found one thing the reviewer did not know: the entry check compares process.argv[1] with import.meta.url, and Node resolves symlinks in import.meta.url but not in process.argv[1]. So when the script is started with an absolute path that goes through a symlink, the check never matches and the script exits 0 without checking anything. The build itself is safe: it starts the script as `node scripts/assert-no-auth-token.mjs` from inside web/, and Node's working folder is always the real path (measured from a symlinked folder: exit 1 on a planted leak). But the test exactly as the finding wrote it starts the copy with an absolute path under Node's temp folder, and on macOS that folder sits behind a system symlink, so that test fails on a Mac.
findings.recorded_decisions: Already a deferred minor in the implementation ledger (Task 2: 'the exit-1 path has no test'); no decision says to leave it untested.

findings.batch: B — tests that prove a guard works
findings.plain_title: Four storage catches: nothing tests which report each one sends
findings.engine_title: Storage-refusal vs bug split unpinned at four storage catches
findings.engine_why_it_matters: Four of the six storage catches decide whether a failure is the visitor's environment (a breadcrumb, no quota) or our bug (an error event), and seven of their eight arms have no assertion. If the check were inverted or the else arm dropped, every settings edit by a private-window or full-quota visitor would send an error event (quota burn, bogus issues), or a real serializer bug would be swallowed as a breadcrumb. web/AGENTS.md says the lint rule cannot see a report made in only one branch of a catch, so nothing else would fail: only transport-storage.ts's two catches have unit cases, and e2e case 5 reaches the settings-read noteError arm alone.
findings.engine_suggested_fix: Add one case per catch that makes storage throw new DOMException('blocked', 'SecurityError') and then new TypeError('our bug'), asserting addBreadcrumb (the catch's message, data.error 'SecurityError') versus captureException, the way transport-storage.test.ts:239-298 does. In PlayerShell.test.tsx: spy Storage.prototype.getItem to throw (settings read), seed '{broken' with setItem throwing (repair write-back), and edit one setting with setItem throwing (edit write). In useRestoredTransport.test.ts: assert the breadcrumb in 'a blocked write-back keeps the restore and the warning' and add the TypeError variant asserting captureException.
findings.engine_validator: The four catches at PlayerShell.tsx:216-218, :246-248, :759-760 and useRestoredTransport.ts:117-119 were bare catch blocks at base 47a7c6c3 and now branch on isStorageRefusal, yet PlayerShell.test.tsx contains no Storage spy, useRestoredTransport.test.ts:226-240 throws QuotaExceededError but asserts nothing about addBreadcrumb or captureException (both mocked globally at vitest.setup.ts:9), only error-reporting.e2e.ts:166-185 asserts the settings-read breadcrumb arm, and web/AGENTS.md:20-22 states lint cannot see a one-branch report, so seven of eight arms are unpinned; the precondition is a future inverted check or dropped arm, so incidence was not measured.
findings.severity_meaning: P2 = a real problem with a meaningful downside; fix if straightforward
findings.confidence_meaning: 75 = the reviewer inferred it from reading the code; this loop's verifier then ran it (see 'verified')
findings.verified: pass — seven of the eight arms (blocked storage -> breadcrumb; our bug -> error report) have no assertion; only e2e case 5 pins the settings-read breadcrumb.
findings.scenario: You tidy one of these catches later, for example you swap its two lines while moving code. From then on, every visitor in a private window who changes a setting sends an error report to Sentry, which uses the 5,000-a-month quota on something that is not a bug; or a real bug in our settings code becomes a quiet breadcrumb. No unit test would fail today: in the spike, the 19 other PlayerShell cases stayed green when any one of these catches was swapped.
findings.whats_wrong: Each of the four catches decides: storage the browser refused (a private window, a full quota) leaves only a breadcrumb (spec decision S2b), anything else is our bug and sends an error report. Nothing tests that split at these four places, and the lint rule cannot see a report made in only one branch (web/AGENTS.md says so).
findings.breaks_today: Nothing today; it guards a future edit. All four catches pick the right arm today: the new cases pass on the current code.

findings.plain_title: The open-a-file error handling is written twice (file picker and drag-and-drop)
findings.engine_title: Open-failure handling duplicated across picker and drop handler
findings.engine_why_it_matters: The picker (OpenFileControl.accept) and the drop handler (PlayerShell.acceptDropped) now each carry the same ~25-line frame: rememberOpenFile, suspendInstruments, a `read` flag, an E101/E102-versus-E105 split with its {type, bytes} facts, the dismiss-and-toast tail, and restoreInstruments in a `finally`. Only comments ('Same boundary as OpenFileControl's accept') and a test written to keep the copies in step (commit f25daa41, 'pin that both open paths remember the file name first') hold the two together, so a copy that misses rememberOpenFile sends the file name unscrubbed from that entry point, and one that misses restoreInstruments leaves the instruments tag off for the rest of the visit (report.ts:156-159 documents that failure mode). One openPickedFile(file, load) helper beside readNotation and loadFailureMessage owns both invariants once and removes the duplicated lines from the 1382-line PlayerShell.tsx.
findings.engine_suggested_fix: In web/app/play/OpenFileControl.tsx (it already exports readNotation, openFailureCode, readFailureMessage, loadFailureMessage and fileType) add `export async function openPickedFile(file: File, load: (notation: LoadedNotation) => Promise<void>): Promise<ErrorCode | null>` that runs rememberOpenFile, suspendInstruments, readNotation, `read = true`, load; in its catch it picks `code = read ? ERROR.openFailedAfterRead : openFailureCode(file)`, calls reportError with level 'warning' only when the file was not read, runs toast.dismiss('notation-load') and toast.error(read ? loadFailureMessage(file) : readFailureMessage(file), { id: `${code}:${file.name}` }), and returns the code; restoreInstruments goes in its `finally`. Then `accept` becomes `void openPickedFile(file, onNotation)` and `acceptDropped` becomes `const code = await openPickedFile(file, requestNotation); if (code) setAnnouncement(`${file.name} could not be opened. Error ${code}.`)`. Assumption: the screen-reader announcement stays drop-only, as today. The E103 catch (PlayerShell.tsx:914-940) and the post-swap E105 catch (PlayerShell.tsx:997-1008) can adopt the same dismiss-and-toast tail later; they need not move now.
findings.engine_validator: At base 47a7c6c3 both handlers held only a short try/catch, and this diff grew PlayerShell.tsx:1051-1079 and OpenFileControl.tsx:93-123 into the same ~25-line frame (rememberOpenFile, suspendInstruments, the read flag with its E105 versus E101/E102 split, the dismiss-and-toast tail also repeated at PlayerShell.tsx:928 and :1003, restoreInstruments in finally) joined only by cross-referencing comments, although per-path tests (OpenFileControl.test.tsx:74,100; PlayerShell.test.tsx:262,349) already pin several of those invariants, so the cited drift consequences are partly guarded and their future incidence was not measured.

spike.problems: 1) The signature in the finding does not compile as written. It types load as returning Promise<void>, but the onNotation prop is typed void | Promise<void> on purpose (its comment explains why). TypeScript gave error TS2345 at the call in accept. The spike types load as void | Promise<void> instead, and leaves the prop type alone. 2) One small change of order, in the picker only: toast.dismiss now runs after the report, not before it. This order is the same as the drop path and as the two other catches in PlayerShell.tsx (E103 and the E105 after the swap), so three of the four old copies already used it. A person cannot see the difference, because both calls run in the same moment. It would matter only if reportError threw: then the picker would now skip the dismiss and the error toast (the drop path already did that). One of the two orders has to change; to keep the picker's old order, move the toast.dismiss line above the reportError lines. 3) Four exports lose their only outside user: readNotation, openFailureCode, readFailureMessage and loadFailureMessage in web/app/play/OpenFileControl.tsx. The repo's knip tool (configured, but not run in CI) now lists them as unused exports. The spike left them exported. Dropping the word export on those four was not tried. 4) The drop path now sets the screen-reader text one small step later than before (after restoreInstruments, not before it). The final text is the same, and no test or scenario can tell. 5) accept stays in OpenFileControl.tsx as a two-line wrapper, because openPickedFile takes a real File and the cancel case (no file) still needs its guard. 6) The stale comment above acceptDropped is replaced: it now names E101, E102 and E105 and says the announcement is the drop path's own. Extra checks, all pass: prettier --check and cspell on the two files.

fyi: Three reviewers (testing, maintainability, reliability) note that the production-only upload gate in web/next.config.ts (VERCEL_ENV === 'production' ? SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN : undefined, plus sourcemaps.disable and the hook flag) has no test, so a later edit back to reading the token alone would pass every gate. The engine filed it as a testing gap, not a finding. A small extracted function with a test, as web/scripts/app-version.mjs does for the same rule, would pin it.

Sentry's Dedupe integration drops an event identical to the previous one; two different non-score files opened back to back fail with the same fixed sentence and stack, so the second E103 (with its file type) never arrives. The same holds for E101 and E102. Counts undercount repeats.
A production deploy whose DSN or token is later deleted or renamed ships green with monitoring silently off; the owner's one-time setup step 6 check is the only guard.

A crafted file with tens of thousands of uniquely named tracks could freeze the tab during the open: the names filter's remember() re-sorts its list for every name (O(n^2 log n)). Crafted files only; nothing leaves the device.
On a return visit to /play in the same tab, a crash before the player's mount effect runs sends the previous visit's instruments tag (a known deferred minor from Task 13).
global-error.tsx's Try again calls reset(); Next 16's bundled guide suggests retry() in most cases. Spec section 2.2 chose reset, and the page also says to reload.
No end-to-end case drives a real render crash to an E901 report, and none proves that text from INSIDE a real file (not only its name) is absent from an E103 report.

The `process.argv[1] === import.meta.url` entry check used by 9 scripts (5 in web/scripts, 4 in tooling) skips its work when a script is started by an absolute path through a symlink (measured). Every build starts them by a relative path, so nothing is affected today; Node 24's import.meta.main would fix all nine. A pre-existing pattern, outside this PR.
The end-to-end lane runs Chromium only, so Firefox and Safari behaviour of the Sentry filter is pinned by unit cases only (relevant to F-4).
